An adjustable square skylight is being expanded as part of a building renovation. The area of the skylight is increasing at a rate of $27{\text{ mm}}^{2}\text{/s}.$ At what rate are the diagonals increasing when each diagonal measures $18\,\text{mm}?$

The diagonal is increasing at a rate of
{{field-1}} $\text{mm/s}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the area of the square skylight, and $h$ be the length of its diagonal. The relationship between $A$ and $h$ is

$$
A=\frac{{h}^{2}}{2}.
$$

We want to find

$$
\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}.
$$

Differentiating the relationship between $A$ and $h$ with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{h}^{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}h}(\frac{{h}^{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}\cdot h \\ \frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{1}{h}\cdot \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the area of the square is increasing at a rate of $27{\text{ mm}}^{2}\text{/s},$ so

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=27.
$$

Also, we want to compute the rate of change of the diagonals when the diagonal has length $h=18.$ Substituting this information into our expression for $\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{1}{18}\cdot 27 \\ \frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{27}{18} \\ \frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} & =1.5\text{ mm/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the diagonal of the skylight is increasing at a rate of 
$1.5\text{ mm/s}.$
